headings: Ask what the food is likely to do
Not every item belongs in a drawer
raw_text:
# The Small Refrigerator Slider That Can Help Fresh Food Last Longer

Inside many refrigerators, a small slider can look unimportant.

But the crisper drawer often has two choices: low humidity and high humidity. These are not just words on a label. They change how air and moisture move around the food.

The low-humidity setting lets more air pass through. The high-humidity setting is more closed, so more moisture stays near the food.

That difference matters because fresh food does not all change in the same way. Some food can lose water and wilt. Other food gives off a natural gas as it ripens. The right setting can give each kind of food a better place to stay fresh.

So the real question is not simply, “Is this a fruit or a vegetable?” The better question is, “What is this food most likely to need?”

### Ask what the food is likely to do

A useful sorting rule is simple: Is the food losing water quickly, or is it releasing a natural gas called ethylene that may make nearby food ripen too fast?

Apples, pears, bananas, and tomatoes fit the second pattern. Leafy greens and broccoli fit the first. Strawberries and oranges are important exceptions. Although they are fruits, they favor high humidity, around 90 to 95 percent.

This question is more useful than putting every fruit or every vegetable in the same setting.

### Not every item belongs in a drawer

The crisper drawer is not the whole storage map. Tomatoes and bananas are recommended for counter storage, rather than refrigeration.

Potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic are different. They do not need refrigeration and are recommended for a cool, dry place.

So “not refrigerated” does not always mean “leave it on the kitchen counter.” Before changing a drawer setting, first check whether the food belongs in the refrigerator at all.

## In one line…

A crisper drawer can help when you match the food’s main risk—not just its name—to the setting, and first check whether it belongs in the refrigerator.
